units.title: Reading stories and poems
units.outcome: read a story or poem and say the main idea and favourite part

lessons.title: The parts of a story
lessons.engage: Show three pictures out of order; learners put them in order and say what happens first, next, last.
lessons.teach: Read the passage aloud. Name the character (Salma), the setting (a quiet beach) and the beginning, middle and end.
lessons.practise: In pairs, fill a three-box story map for the passage.
lessons.check: Each learner says one sentence about the end of the story.

lessons.title: Who, what, where, when, why
lessons.engage: Ask five quick questions about the classroom; learners answer in full sentences.
lessons.teach: Teach the five question words and what kind of answer each one wants. Model finding the answer in the text with a finger.
lessons.practise: Learners answer six questions about the passage, underlining the line that proves each answer.
lessons.check: Swap papers and check one answer together.

lessons.title: Main idea and favourite part
lessons.engage: Ask: if you told a friend this story in one sentence, what would you say?
lessons.teach: Teach main idea (the big point) against details (small facts). Model one main idea sentence for the passage.
lessons.practise: Learners write the main idea and draw their favourite part with a caption.
lessons.check: Share captions; the class votes for the clearest main idea sentence.

lessons.title: Reading a poem aloud
lessons.engage: Clap the beat of a nursery rhyme together.
lessons.teach: Read a short poem twice: first for meaning, then for rhythm. Point out rhyming words.
lessons.practise: Learners find rhyming pairs and practise reading in groups, then perform one verse.
lessons.check: Each group performs; the class gives one kind compliment and one tip.

lessons.title: Retell and respond
lessons.engage: Pass a soft ball; each learner adds one sentence to a class retelling.
lessons.teach: Teach retelling with first, then, next, finally.
lessons.practise: Learners retell the passage in their own words to a partner, then write four sentences.
lessons.check: Read aloud one retelling; check it has a beginning, middle and end.

worksheet.q: Where did Salma live?
Who helped Salma fly the kite?
What colour was the kite?
Why did the kite float away?
worksheet.a: The string slipped from Salma's hand.

worksheet.q: How did Salma feel when she lost the kite?
worksheet.a: Upset; she wanted to cry (accept sad or worried).

worksheet.q: Where did they find the kite?
worksheet.a: Caught on a low palm branch.

worksheet.q: Write the main idea of the story in one sentence.
worksheet.a: A girl and her grandfather find a lost kite and she learns to hold the string more safely. (Accept any sentence with the same meaning.)

worksheet.q: What will Salma do next time?
worksheet.a: Wrap the string around her wrist.

worksheet.q: Put these events in the order they happened: (a) Salma frees the kite. (b) The string slips away. (c) They follow the kite along the shore.
worksheet.a: b, c, a (the string slips away; they follow the kite along the shore; Salma frees the kite).

worksheet.q: Find two words in the story that name a place.
worksheet.a: Beach, water, shore, palm branch (any two).

bank.q: Name the character and the setting of a story you know.
bank.a: Any correct character and setting, written in a full sentence.

bank.q: Which word rhymes with "beach": reach, bend, bell?
What is the "main idea" of a text?
bank.a: The big point the whole text is about.

bank.q: Write one sentence that begins with "Finally".
bank.a: Any sentence beginning with "Finally" with a capital letter and full stop.

units.subject: ENG
units.title: Subject and predicate
units.outcome: find who or what a sentence is about and what it says about it

lessons.title: What makes a sentence?
lessons.engage: Write "ran the dog" on the board; ask if it makes sense and how to fix it.
lessons.teach: Teach: a sentence tells a complete idea, starts with a capital letter and ends with . ? or !.
lessons.practise: Learners sort cards into sentences and non-sentences and fix three.
lessons.check: Write one sentence about today's weather.

lessons.title: The subject
lessons.engage: Say "The cat sat on the mat"; ask who or what the sentence is about.
lessons.teach: Teach: the subject is who or what the sentence is about. Underline the subject in five model sentences.
lessons.practise: Learners underline the subject in ten sentences.
lessons.check: Quick poll: each learner shares one subject.

lessons.title: The predicate
lessons.engage: Cover the subject in a sentence; ask what is left.
lessons.teach: Teach: the predicate tells what the subject does or is. Draw a line between subject and predicate in model sentences.
lessons.practise: Learners draw the line in ten sentences and colour the subject blue and the predicate green.
lessons.check: Exit ticket: split one sentence of their own.

lessons.title: Build and join
lessons.engage: Give each learner half a sentence on a card; they walk to find their match.
lessons.teach: Teach: every sentence needs both parts; show how adding detail grows each part.
lessons.practise: Learners build six full sentences from a subject bank and a predicate bank, then write two of their own.
lessons.check: Read two sentences aloud; the class decides which part is the subject.

lessons.title: Practice and review
lessons.engage: Mini-whiteboard quiz: subject or predicate?
lessons.teach: Review with a game of "sentence builders".

worksheet.q: Underline the subject: The red kite flew high.
Underline the subject: My little brother sleeps late.
Underline the predicate: The children sang a song.
Underline the predicate: Grandfather planted a palm tree.
Is this a sentence? "Runs fast the horse." Write Yes or No and fix it.
Join each subject to a predicate to make two full sentences. Subjects: The baker; Birds. Predicates: fly south; bakes bread.
worksheet.a: The baker bakes bread. Birds fly south.

worksheet.q: Write the sentence correctly: the camel drank water
Add a subject: ______ jumped over the fence.
worksheet.a: Any sensible subject, for example "The goat".

worksheet.q: Add a predicate: The tall teacher ______ .
worksheet.a: Any sensible predicate, for example "walked into the room".

worksheet.q: Write one sentence of your own and draw a line between the subject and the predicate.
worksheet.a: Any correct sentence with the line in the right place.

bank.q: Underline the subject: Our class visited the museum.
Underline the predicate: Dolphins swim in the sea.
Which punctuation mark ends a question?
Write a sentence about a camel. Circle the subject.
bank.a: Any correct sentence about a camel with the subject circled.

units.subject: ENG
units.title: Nouns, pronouns and adjectives
units.outcome: use them correctly and for variety

lessons.title: Naming words
lessons.engage: Play "I spy" with nouns in the room.
lessons.teach: Teach nouns for people, animals, places and things. Common nouns are general; proper nouns name one and start with a capital letter.
lessons.practise: Sort twenty words into common and proper nouns.
lessons.check: Write three proper nouns about our town.

lessons.title: Pronouns
lessons.engage: Read a short paragraph with the same name repeated; ask what sounds odd.
lessons.teach: Teach pronouns: he, she, it, they, we, I, you, and how they stand in for nouns.
lessons.practise: Replace repeated nouns with pronouns in a short text.
lessons.check: Write two sentences using she and they.

lessons.title: Adjectives
lessons.engage: Describe a mystery object in a bag using only words about how it looks and feels.
lessons.teach: Teach adjectives as words that describe nouns; place before the noun and after is or are.
lessons.practise: Add adjectives to ten plain sentences to make them richer.
lessons.check: Write a four-line description of a desert animal.

lessons.title: Putting it together
lessons.engage: Word-class sort game in teams.
lessons.teach: Teach how to spot all three in one sentence.
lessons.practise: Colour nouns blue, pronouns red and adjectives green in a short text.
lessons.check: Exit ticket: write one sentence with all three.

worksheet.q: Circle the proper noun: dog, Dubai, city
Circle the common noun: Monday, teacher, Sara
Write the proper noun for: a country you know.
worksheet.a: Any country name with a capital letter.

worksheet.q: Replace the noun with a pronoun: Omar is tall. ___ is tall.
Replace the noun with a pronoun: The girls ran home. ___ ran home.
Underline the adjective: The sandy beach was warm.
Add an adjective: I saw a ______ camel.
Write the sentence with capitals: sara and maryam live in abu dhabi.
worksheet.a: Sara and Maryam live in Abu Dhabi.

worksheet.q: Which word is a pronoun? Table, she, quickly
Write a sentence using the adjective "shiny".

bank.q: Write one proper noun and one common noun.
bank.a: A capitalised proper noun and a common noun in lower case.

bank.q: Underline the pronoun: She likes dates.
Name two adjectives that describe the sun.
bank.a: Any two, for example hot, bright.

units.subject: ENG
units.title: Verbs and simple tenses
units.outcome: use present, past and future verbs correctly

lessons.title: Action words
lessons.engage: Act out verbs from a hat for the class to guess.
lessons.teach: Teach verbs as words for actions and states (run, is).
lessons.check: Write three sentences with strong verbs.

lessons.title: Present and past
lessons.engage: Show "today we walk" and "yesterday we walked".
lessons.teach: Teach how most verbs add -ed for the past and the common irregular verbs (go-went, see-saw, eat-ate).
lessons.practise: Change ten present sentences to the past.

lessons.title: Future with will
lessons.engage: Ask learners what they will do tomorrow.
lessons.teach: Teach will + verb for the future.
lessons.practise: Write a plan for next weekend with five sentences.

lessons.title: Matching the verb to the subject
lessons.engage: Read "She like" and "They likes"; ask which sounds wrong.
lessons.teach: Teach that singular subjects take -s (She likes) and plural do not (They like).

lessons.check: Share results with a drawing and a sentence.

lessons.title: Plants we use
lessons.engage: Make a class shopping list of plant things we use.
lessons.teach: Teach food, cloth, wood and medicine from plants, and why date palms matter in the UAE.
lessons.check: Choose a plant and say three ways it helps us.

worksheet.q: Which part of a plant takes in water from the soil?
What do leaves make for the plant?
Name three things a plant needs to grow.
worksheet.a: Any three of: light, water, air, space, warmth.

worksheet.q: Put the life cycle in order: seedling, seed, flower, adult plant.
Name two ways seeds can travel.
worksheet.a: Any two of: wind, water, animals, bursting pods.

worksheet.q: Why does the stem matter?
worksheet.a: It holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves.

worksheet.q: What is a fair test?
worksheet.a: A test where only one thing changes and the others stay the same.

worksheet.q: A plant is kept in a dark cupboard. What will probably happen? Why?
worksheet.a: It grows weak and pale because it has no light to make food.

worksheet.q: Which part of a plant makes seeds?
Draw and label a plant with four parts.
worksheet.a: Marked with the labelling rubric: roots, stem, leaves, flower correctly placed and labelled.

bank.q: Name one fruit that has seeds you can see.
bank.a: Any, for example apple, orange, melon.

bank.q: What is germination?
bank.a: When a seed starts to grow into a new plant.

bank.q: Why do plants need sunlight?

units.subject: SCI
units.title: Animal life and adaptation
units.outcome: link body features to habitats including desert and sea

lessons.title: Animal groups
lessons.engage: Show cards with animals; sort them any way.
lessons.teach: Teach five groups by body covering and how they breathe and reproduce: mammals (fur or hair, feed milk), birds (feathers, eggs), reptiles (dry scales), fish (gills, scales), insects (six legs).
lessons.practise: Sort twenty animal cards and record in a table.

lessons.title: Habitats
lessons.engage: Show pictures of desert, sea, forest and polar places.
lessons.teach: Teach that a habitat gives food, water and shelter.
lessons.practise: Match animals to habitats and say why.

lessons.title: Adaptation
lessons.engage: Ask why a camel can live in the desert.
lessons.teach: Teach adaptation using a camel (humps store fat, wide feet, long eyelashes), a fish (gills, fins), a bird (wings, light bones).
lessons.practise: Choose two animals and match body parts to jobs.
lessons.check: Explain one adaptation to a partner.

lessons.title: What animals eat
lessons.engage: Show teeth pictures of a cow and a lion.
lessons.teach: Teach herbivore, carnivore and omnivore, and teeth shapes.

worksheet.q: Name an animal with feathers.
worksheet.a: Any bird, for example falcon or parrot.

worksheet.q: Is a snake a mammal, a bird or a reptile?
Give one adaptation of a camel and say how it helps.
worksheet.a: For example: wide feet stop it sinking in sand; the hump stores fat for energy.

worksheet.q: What do all habitats provide?
Match: herbivore, carnivore, omnivore with: eats only plants, eats only meat, eats both.
worksheet.a: Herbivore eats only plants; carnivore eats only meat; omnivore eats both.

worksheet.q: Name one animal that lives in the sea and one that lives in the desert.
worksheet.a: Sea: for example shark or turtle. Desert: for example camel or oryx.

worksheet.q: How many legs does an insect have?
Why do fish have gills?
worksheet.a: To take oxygen from the water.

worksheet.q: Complete the food chain: grass → ___ → lion.
worksheet.a: An animal that eats grass, for example zebra.

worksheet.q: Draw an animal and label two parts that help it survive.

bank.q: Name a mammal that lives in water.
What is a habitat?
bank.a: The natural home of a plant or animal.

bank.q: Is a lion a herbivore or a carnivore?

units.subject: SCI
units.title: Food and digestion
units.outcome: group nutrients and describe the journey of food

lessons.title: Food groups
lessons.engage: Bring a lunchbox sort.
lessons.teach: Teach the groups: energy foods, body-building foods, protective foods, and water.

lessons.title: A healthy plate
lessons.engage: Show an unhealthy lunch and ask what to change.
lessons.teach: Teach portions: half fruit and vegetables, a quarter grains, a quarter protein.
lessons.practise: Draw a plate for breakfast, lunch and dinner.

lessons.title: The journey of food
lessons.engage: Roll a ball through a long tube as a model.
lessons.teach: Teach mouth, food pipe, stomach, small intestine, large intestine.
lessons.practise: Label the digestive path and write what happens at each part.
lessons.check: Explain the journey in three sentences.

lessons.title: Teeth and care
lessons.engage: Look at your teeth in mirrors and count them.
lessons.teach: Teach tooth types (incisors cut, canines tear, molars grind) and caring for teeth.
lessons.practise: Draw a tooth map and make a brushing plan.

worksheet.q: Name two foods that give energy.
worksheet.a: Any two of: rice, bread, pasta, potatoes.

worksheet.q: Name one body-building food.
worksheet.a: Any of: fish, eggs, beans, meat, milk.

worksheet.q: Why do we need water?
worksheet.a: To stay healthy, move food through the body and keep us cool.

worksheet.q: Where does digestion start?
Put in order: stomach, mouth, small intestine, food pipe.
worksheet.a: Mouth, food pipe, stomach, small intestine.

worksheet.q: Which teeth are used for grinding?
Write two ways to care for your teeth.
worksheet.a: For example: brush twice a day; eat less sugar; visit the dentist.

worksheet.q: Write a healthy breakfast.
worksheet.a: Any balanced breakfast with at least two food groups.

worksheet.q: What does fibre help with?
Is a chocolate bar a healthy daily snack? Give a reason.
worksheet.a: No; it has a lot of sugar and fat. Accept a reasoned answer.

bank.q: Which part of the body breaks food into small pieces first?
Name one fruit and one vegetable.
How many times a day should we brush our teeth?

units.subject: SCI
units.title: Rocks, soil and water
units.outcome: compare soils and describe how water is used and saved

lessons.title: Rocks
lessons.engage: Hold a smooth and a rough rock.
lessons.teach: Teach properties: hard, soft, rough, smooth, heavy, light. Rocks are used for building.
lessons.practise: Test and sort rocks by properties.

lessons.title: Soil
lessons.engage: Dig up a spoon of soil in a clear cup.
lessons.teach: Teach soil as bits of rock plus humus; sand, clay and loam.
lessons.practise: Shake soil with water in a jar and observe layers.

lessons.title: Where water comes from
lessons.engage: Show a water bottle label.
lessons.teach: Teach sources: rain, rivers, wells, sea water made drinkable by desalination in the UAE.
lessons.practise: Draw the journey of water to our home.

lessons.title: Saving water
lessons.engage: Compare a dripping tap and a closed one.
lessons.teach: Teach ways to save water at home and school.
lessons.practise: Create a poster and a class water pledge.
lessons.check: Count how many saving ideas we have.

worksheet.q: Name two properties of rocks.
worksheet.a: Any two, for example hard, rough.

worksheet.q: Which soil holds the most water: sand or clay?
Why do plants grow better in soil with humus?
worksheet.a: Humus has nutrients that help plants grow.

worksheet.q: Name two sources of water.
worksheet.a: Any two of: rain, rivers, wells, the sea (after desalination).

worksheet.q: What does desalination do?
worksheet.a: Removes salt from sea water so we can use it.

worksheet.q: Write three ways to save water at home.
worksheet.a: For example: close the tap; take short showers; fix leaks.

worksheet.q: What happens to sand in a jar of water when you shake it and wait?
worksheet.a: It settles at the bottom first (heavier particles settle first).

worksheet.q: Why are rocks used to build houses?
Is water a renewable or a limited resource? Explain in one sentence.
worksheet.a: It cycles but fresh water is limited, so we must conserve it.

worksheet.q: Draw soil layers and label them.

bank.q: Name one use of rock.
What is soil made of?
bank.a: Tiny bits of rock and humus.

bank.q: Give one way to save water at school.

units.subject: SCI
units.title: Light and shadows
units.outcome: explain how shadows form and how they change in length

lessons.title: Sources of light
lessons.engage: Turn off the lights and show a torch.
lessons.teach: Teach natural and made light sources and that the moon reflects the sun.

lessons.title: Which materials let light through?
lessons.engage: Show glass, tissue paper and wood.
lessons.teach: Teach transparent, translucent and opaque.
lessons.practise: Test materials with a torch and record.

lessons.title: Shadows
lessons.engage: Make hand shadows on the wall.
lessons.teach: Teach shadows form when an opaque thing blocks light.
lessons.practise: Draw where a shadow falls when the light comes from the left.

lessons.title: Shadows and the sun
lessons.engage: Measure a shadow stick at 9, 12 and 3.
lessons.teach: Teach that shadows are long in the morning, short at noon and long again.

worksheet.q: Name one natural and one made source of light.
worksheet.a: Natural: the sun. Made: a torch or a lamp.

worksheet.q: Is the moon a source of light?
worksheet.a: No. It reflects light from the sun.

worksheet.q: Which is transparent: glass, wood or tissue paper?
A plastic sheet lets some light through but you cannot see clearly. What word describes it?
What is needed to make a shadow?
worksheet.a: A light source, an opaque object and a surface.

worksheet.q: When is a shadow shortest in the day?
Why are curtains made of opaque cloth in a bedroom?
worksheet.a: To block light so the room is dark.

worksheet.q: A torch is moved closer to a toy. What happens to the shadow?
Draw the shadow of a tree when the sun is low.
worksheet.a: A long shadow on the side away from the sun.

worksheet.q: Write one safety rule when using light.
worksheet.a: For example: never look straight at the sun.

bank.q: Name an opaque object.
bank.a: Any, for example a book or wood.

bank.q: Why do we see a shadow on the ground?
Name one light source.
bank.a: Any, for example the sun or a candle.

units.subject: SCI
units.title: Forces and motion
units.outcome: describe pushes and pulls and the effect of friction

lessons.title: Pushes and pulls
lessons.engage: Open and close a door.
lessons.teach: Teach forces as pushes and pulls that start, stop or change a motion.
lessons.practise: Sort actions into pushes and pulls.

lessons.title: Friction
lessons.engage: Slide a block across carpet, wood and a tray.
lessons.teach: Teach friction between surfaces and how rough surfaces cause more.

lessons.title: Gravity
lessons.engage: Drop a ball and a sheet of paper.
lessons.teach: Teach gravity as the pull toward the Earth that makes things fall.
lessons.check: Discuss why we do not float away.

lessons.title: Magnets
lessons.engage: Test which objects a magnet picks up.
lessons.teach: Teach magnets attract iron and steel and have poles that attract or repel.

worksheet.q: Is kicking a ball a push or a pull?
Is opening a drawer by the handle a push or a pull?
Which surface gives more friction: ice or sand paper?
What force makes a dropped ball fall?
Name one material that a magnet attracts.
worksheet.a: Iron or steel (for example a paper clip).

worksheet.q: When two north poles are brought together, do they attract or repel?
Why do we put grip on sports shoes?
worksheet.a: To increase friction so we do not slip.

worksheet.q: Which is faster down a slope: a car on carpet or on a smooth table?
worksheet.a: On the smooth table because there is less friction.

worksheet.q: Name two things a force can do to a moving object.
worksheet.a: Any two of: speed it up, slow it down, stop it, change its direction.

worksheet.q: Write a prediction for a ball rolling on sand and on tile.
worksheet.a: The ball rolls farther on tile because there is less friction.

bank.q: Name one force.
Does a magnet attract wood?
What does friction do to a moving thing?

units.subject: SCI
units.title: Weather and the sky
units.outcome: link the sun, moon and weather to daily and seasonal change

lessons.title: Day and night
lessons.engage: Shine a torch on a globe and spin it.
lessons.teach: Teach Earth spins once every day, giving day and night.

lessons.title: The moon
lessons.engage: Show moon phase pictures.
lessons.teach: Teach the moon changes shape because we see different parts lit by the sun.
lessons.check: Draw the moon for one week.

lessons.title: Weather
lessons.engage: Look outside and describe today's weather.
lessons.teach: Teach describing weather: sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy, hot, cool; reading a thermometer.
lessons.practise: Record a weather chart for a week.

lessons.title: Seasons and clothes
lessons.engage: Ask what we wear in hot and cool weather.
lessons.teach: Teach that there are four seasons in many places and the UAE has a hot summer and a mild winter.
lessons.practise: Match clothes and activities to seasons.

worksheet.q: What causes day and night?
worksheet.a: The Earth spins on its axis.

worksheet.q: Does the sun move around the Earth or does the Earth spin?
worksheet.a: The Earth spins (it only looks as if the sun moves).

worksheet.q: Name two kinds of weather.
worksheet.a: Any two, for example sunny and windy.

worksheet.q: What do we use to measure temperature?
What clothes do we wear in hot weather?
worksheet.a: Light, loose clothes and a hat.

worksheet.q: Is the moon a star?
worksheet.a: No. It is a natural satellite of the Earth.

worksheet.q: Why do we see different shapes of the moon?
worksheet.a: Because we see different parts of the lit side as it moves around the Earth.

worksheet.q: Which season is the hottest in the UAE?
Record: if it is 38 °C, is it hot or cool?
Draw the weather you saw today and write a caption.
worksheet.a: Any correct drawing and a full-sentence caption.

bank.q: Name a measuring tool for rainfall.
How long does the Earth take to spin once?
Name one planet.
bank.a: Any, for example Earth or Mars.

units.subject: SST
units.title: The United Arab Emirates
units.outcome: locate the seven emirates, describe leaders, symbols, landmarks and heritage

lessons.title: Where are we?
lessons.engage: Show a world map and find the UAE.
lessons.teach: Teach the UAE is a country in the Arabian Peninsula by the Gulf.
lessons.practise: Point to the UAE and neighbours on a map.

lessons.title: The seven emirates
lessons.engage: Chant the names with a rhythm.
lessons.teach: Teach the seven: Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah; Abu Dhabi is the capital.

lessons.title: The flag and symbols
lessons.engage: Show the flag and ask what the colours may mean.
lessons.teach: Teach the four colours (red, green, white and black), the falcon as national bird, the Arabian oryx as national animal and the ghaf tree.
lessons.practise: Draw the flag; match symbols to pictures.

lessons.title: How the UAE began
lessons.engage: Show a timeline from the 1960s to 1971.
lessons.teach: Teach that seven emirates joined on 2 December 1971 and the Founding Father led this union.

lessons.title: People who lead
lessons.engage: Role-play a class council.
lessons.teach: Teach the roles of rulers and the President in simple words.
lessons.check: Write one question for a leader.

lessons.title: Famous places
lessons.engage: Show landmark photos.
lessons.teach: Teach landmarks: Burj Khalifa, Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque, Louvre Abu Dhabi, Jebel Jais.

lessons.title: National Day project
lessons.engage: Plan a celebration.
lessons.teach: Teach how people celebrate with respect and unity.

worksheet.q: How many emirates make up the UAE?
Name the capital of the UAE.
Name three emirates.
When did the seven emirates form one country?
Name the four colours of the UAE flag.
What is the national bird of the UAE?
What is the currency of the UAE?
In which emirate is the Burj Khalifa?
Name one national symbol besides the flag.
worksheet.a: Falcon, Arabian oryx or ghaf tree.

worksheet.q: Why is unity important for a country?
worksheet.a: People can work together, feel safe and share what they have.

bank.q: Which emirate has the capital city of the UAE?
What is the UAE National Day date?
Name one UAE landmark.

units.subject: SST
units.title: Maps and directions
units.outcome: read a simple map using a key and compass points

lessons.title: What is a map?
lessons.engage: Look at a treasure map.
lessons.teach: Teach that a map is a drawing of a place from above.
lessons.practise: Draw a map of our classroom.

lessons.title: Map keys and symbols
lessons.engage: Match symbols to places.
lessons.teach: Teach reading a key.
lessons.practise: Complete a key for a school map.

lessons.title: The compass
lessons.engage: Stand in the playground and find north.
lessons.teach: Teach N, S, E and W.
lessons.practise: Label a compass rose and follow directions on a grid.

lessons.title: Routes and directions
lessons.engage: Walk the route to the library.
lessons.teach: Teach giving and following directions.
lessons.practise: Write steps from the gate to the classroom.

worksheet.q: What is a map?
worksheet.a: A drawing of a place as seen from above.

worksheet.q: What does a map key show?
worksheet.a: What the symbols on the map mean.

worksheet.q: Name the four main directions.
If you face north and turn right, which direction do you face?
If you walk south, which direction is behind you?
Draw a symbol for a hospital and a school.
worksheet.a: Any clear symbols with a key.

worksheet.q: Write directions from your classroom to the school office.
worksheet.a: Marked with the directions checklist: start point, left/right and landmarks, end point.

worksheet.q: Which tool tells us where north is?
Why do maps use symbols?
worksheet.a: To show lots of information in small space.

worksheet.q: Draw a simple map of your street.
worksheet.a: Marked with the map rubric: title, key, compass.

bank.q: What do we call the small drawing that shows directions on a map?
Which direction is opposite to east?
Name one thing a key can show.
bank.a: Any, for example a road or a school.

units.subject: SST
units.title: Communities and helpers
units.outcome: describe how people work together and why services matter

lessons.title: Our community
lessons.engage: Draw your neighbourhood.
lessons.teach: Teach a community as people living and working together.
lessons.practise: List places and people in our community.

lessons.title: Community helpers
lessons.engage: Mime a helper for others to guess.
lessons.teach: Teach the jobs of doctors, police, firefighters, teachers, waste collectors.

lessons.title: Services we share
lessons.engage: List things we all use, such as roads and water.
lessons.teach: Teach public services and how they are paid for by all.

lessons.title: Working together
lessons.engage: Build a tower in teams.
lessons.teach: Teach cooperation and fair rules.

worksheet.q: Name three community helpers.
worksheet.a: Any three, for example doctor, police officer, teacher.

worksheet.q: Who helps us when there is a fire?
Who looks after sick people?
Why do we need rules in a community?
worksheet.a: So that people are safe and treated fairly.

worksheet.q: Name two public places we all share.
Write a thank-you sentence to a helper.
worksheet.a: Any polite sentence naming the helper and the thanks.

worksheet.q: How can you help keep your neighbourhood clean?
worksheet.a: For example put rubbish in bins; pick up litter.

worksheet.q: Why do people cooperate?
worksheet.a: Working together gets more done and is fairer.

worksheet.q: What number do you call in an emergency in the UAE?
Draw your favourite community helper at work.
worksheet.a: Any relevant drawing with a label.

bank.q: Which helper teaches children?
Name one shared service.
What does cooperate mean?

units.subject: SST
units.title: Heritage and traditions
units.outcome: describe traditional life in the Gulf and what we keep today

lessons.title: Life in the past
lessons.engage: Show old photos of the Gulf.
lessons.teach: Teach how people lived by the sea and in the desert.
lessons.practise: Make a two-column chart of then and now.

lessons.title: Traditions we keep
lessons.engage: Taste dates and Arabic coffee if allowed, else show pictures.
lessons.teach: Teach hospitality, the majlis, falconry and the souq.
lessons.practise: Write a postcard about a tradition.

lessons.title: Heritage project
lessons.engage: Plan a heritage corner.
lessons.teach: Teach respect for heritage places.

worksheet.q: Name two traditional jobs in the Gulf.
worksheet.a: Any two, for example pearl diver, fisher.

worksheet.q: What is a dhow?
What is a majlis?
worksheet.a: A place where people gather to talk and welcome guests.

worksheet.q: What fruit comes from the date palm?
Name one tradition that people still keep.
Why is heritage important?
worksheet.a: It teaches us about our past and who we are.

worksheet.q: How are souqs different from malls?
worksheet.a: Souqs are traditional markets with small shops; malls are large modern buildings. Accept a fair comparison.

worksheet.q: Draw a dhow on the sea.
Name one thing people used before electricity to keep cool.
worksheet.a: For example wind towers or shade.

worksheet.q: Write two sentences about your family's traditions.

bank.q: What did pearl divers look for?
Name a traditional drink offered to guests.
What does heritage mean?
bank.a: Things from the past that we keep and value.

units.subject: COM
units.title: Pictures and shapes in a drawing program
units.outcome: rotate, resize, colour and save a picture

lessons.title: Opening a drawing program
lessons.engage: Show a finished picture.
lessons.teach: Teach opening, naming and saving a file.
lessons.check: Show a file in the folder.

lessons.title: Shape and line tools
lessons.engage: Draw shapes on paper.
lessons.teach: Teach the shape tools, line tool, colours and fill.

lessons.title: Brush and eraser
lessons.engage: Free draw.
lessons.teach: Teach brush sizes and the eraser.

lessons.title: Rotate, flip and resize
lessons.engage: Show a picture and rotate it.
lessons.teach: Teach rotate, flip and resize.

lessons.title: Select, copy and paste
lessons.engage: Ask how to draw ten stars quickly.
lessons.teach: Teach selecting and copying parts.

lessons.title: Colour mixing and gradients
lessons.engage: Mix paint on paper.
lessons.teach: Teach the colour picker and mixing in the program.

lessons.title: Project
lessons.engage: Plan a picture.
lessons.teach: Teach planning with a sketch.
lessons.practise: Make a final picture with title.

worksheet.q: What does the "undo" button do?
worksheet.a: It takes back the last thing you did.

worksheet.q: How do you save a picture?
worksheet.a: Choose Save, type a name and pick a folder.

worksheet.q: Which tool fills a closed shape with colour?
What does "rotate" do to a picture?
What does "flip" do?
Name two shape tools.
worksheet.a: Any two, for example rectangle, circle.

worksheet.q: How can we make a picture bigger without losing its shape?
worksheet.a: Resize while keeping the sides in proportion.

worksheet.q: Why do we give a file a clear name?
worksheet.a: So we can find it later.

worksheet.q: Draw and save a picture of a house with three shapes.
worksheet.a: Observe: shapes, colours, saved file with a name.

worksheet.q: Write one tip you would give a friend about the drawing program.

bank.q: What is a pixel?
bank.a: A tiny dot that makes up a picture on the screen.

bank.q: Which key combination copies?
Name one use of the eraser.
bank.a: To remove marks you do not want.

units.subject: COM
units.title: Typing and word processing basics
units.outcome: type a short text and format it

lessons.title: Hands on the keys
lessons.engage: Show a keyboard map.
lessons.teach: Teach posture and the home row.

lessons.title: Typing words and sentences
lessons.engage: Race to type a short word.
lessons.teach: Teach capitals with shift and punctuation.

lessons.title: Making text look good
lessons.engage: Compare plain and formatted text.
lessons.teach: Teach font, size, bold and colour.

lessons.title: Save and print
lessons.engage: Show a printed page.
lessons.teach: Teach save as, folders and print preview.
lessons.practise: Save a document in a folder.

worksheet.q: Which row has the keys A S D F?
What does the space bar do?
How do you make a capital letter?
worksheet.a: Hold the shift key and press the letter.

worksheet.q: What does backspace do?
worksheet.a: Deletes the letter behind the cursor.

worksheet.q: Which button makes text darker and thicker?
Type your name and the date.
worksheet.a: Observe: capital letters and a saved document.

worksheet.q: Why should we sit up straight when we type?
worksheet.a: To protect our back and wrists and type better.

worksheet.q: What is a font?
Where do you find the print button?
worksheet.a: In the File menu or on the toolbar.

worksheet.q: Type three sentences about your school and save.

bank.q: What key moves to a new line?
Name one font you can use.
How do you make text bigger?

units.subject: COM
units.title: Algorithms and loops without a computer
units.outcome: write and test a sequence of steps with a repeat

lessons.title: What is an algorithm?
lessons.engage: Give a robot-partner instructions to make a sandwich.
lessons.teach: Teach algorithm as a set of steps in order.

lessons.title: Giving clear instructions
lessons.engage: Guide a partner through a maze on the floor.
lessons.teach: Teach clear short instructions with arrows.
lessons.practise: Write an algorithm for a grid.

lessons.title: Loops
lessons.engage: Show repeating dance moves.
lessons.teach: Teach a loop as repeating steps (repeat 4 times).

lessons.title: Finding bugs
lessons.engage: Give a wrong algorithm.
lessons.teach: Teach debugging: test, find the error, fix.

lessons.title: Mini challenge
lessons.engage: Design a dance.
lessons.teach: Teach combining sequence and loops.

worksheet.q: What is an algorithm?
worksheet.a: A set of steps in order to do a task.

worksheet.q: Put the steps in order: put on socks, wake up, put on shoes.
worksheet.a: Wake up, put on socks, put on shoes.

worksheet.q: What does "repeat 3 times" tell us to do?
Rewrite with a loop: step, step, step, step.
What is a bug in an algorithm?
Find the bug: Draw a square: forward, turn, forward, turn, forward.
worksheet.a: One side and turn are missing; it needs four sides.

worksheet.q: Write four steps for drawing a triangle with arrows.
worksheet.a: Any correct steps ending in a closed triangle.

worksheet.q: Why must instructions be exact?
worksheet.a: So the machine or partner does what we intend.

worksheet.q: Draw an arrow path on a grid from A to B.
